rules.statement: No logo, brand mark, trademark-like symbol, mascot of a company, or platform icon is visible anywhere.
rules.used_by: every asset, concept, duo, and the face-on-head pose sheet (C4), the I4 hair front and its T1 views, and the Gate 2 per-character composite (face on head + hair front)

rules.statement: Nothing depicts or closely imitates a well-known character from games, anime, films, cartoons or toys.
rules.used_by: concept, prints, badges, accessories, duo, and the face-on-head pose sheet (C4), the I4 hair front and its T1 views, and the Gate 2 per-character composite (a signature hairstyle plus face is the likeliest anime look-alike, so it is caught before BUILD, not first at export)

rules.statement: No letters, numbers, words or letter-like marks (in any script) are visible.
rules.used_by: every asset, including the face pose sheet, hair front and Gate 2 composite

rules.statement: Torso and hips are covered by clothing or by a plain base layer, as everyday casual wear; nothing is suggestive, revealing, violent, or crude, and no hate or drug symbols appear.
rules.used_by: concept, garments on the render, duo

rules.statement: The figures keep the blocky body from the guide: a cube head, a box torso, and straight box arms and legs.
The left figure shows a flat 2D anime-style face (eyes and mouth) on the front of the cube head.
The right figure is seen from behind: no eyes or mouth are visible, and the back of the hair and clothing is shown.
Both figures wear the same outfit, hair colour, hairstyle and accessories.
Clothing is flat artwork on the boxes; nothing (skirt, cape, sleeve, ruffle) sticks out past the body boxes.
The hair stays within about one head-height below the head and within one head-width to each side.
The only accessories visible are: {accessory list}.
The design reads clearly at a glance; there are no scattered small decorations.
The two characters look like they belong to the same world (matching drawing style and related colours or motifs).
The two characters are easy to tell apart at a glance by hair shape and outfit.
rules.hard_note: clone band is code; this is the backstop

rules.statement: {anchor} is visible on both characters in the front views.
Character B does not wear {A signature item} and character A does not wear {B signature item}.
rules.note: Code builds the item lists from the spec: only items one character has and the other does not, minus the shared anchors and whatever the structure profile shares on purpose (for `same_club`, the shared main colour and the shared anchors). With an empty list the rule is skipped

rules.statement: Exactly one graphic is shown, whole and centred, with empty space around it.
The graphic depicts {motif}.
The graphic is flat, straight-on artwork, not drawn on clothing or in perspective.
At this small size (the 100-px version), the motif is still recognisable.
The graphic matches the print in the reference crop in motif and colours.
rules.used_by: I2, R2 (when a concept crop exists)

rules.statement: Only one {part} is shown, with no other facial features, skin or head.
The {part} is drawn straight-on (front view), not tilted or in three-quarter view.
The {part}'s outer end is at the right side of the image and its inner end toward the centre-left.
All lines of the {part} are one single flat colour.
The iris has no white highlight dots or shine marks.
Lines are thick and chunky, with no hair-thin strokes.
The line weight and shapes match the style sheet's face parts.
The {part} matches this description: {grammar phrase}.
In the blink render, no iris or eye-white is visible; only the eyelid shows.
Ignoring the white highlight dots and the mouth, the two eyes and brows are mirror images in shape and position.
rules.note: catchlights are deliberately not mirrored, D26/FACE-04, and some mouths are asymmetric

rules.statement: On every skin tone shown, the lash lines, brows and mouth are clearly visible.
In every pose, the painted features keep their shape (no stretching or tearing).
The happy render looks happy and the sad render looks sad.
The face matches the reference face crop in eye shape, iris style, brows and mouth.
rules.note: the neutral render beside the concept face crop; R1, the default face route, is text-only and never sees the concept face, so this is where drift shows up
rules.hard_note: shown after the first choice; the fix offered to the user, never run automatically: I3 guided by the concept crop, or a spec patch

rules.statement: The grey head keeps its exact cube shape, size and position.
No eyes, mouth or other facial features are drawn.
The hair is seen straight-on from the front, level and without perspective.
If there are bangs, they end above where the eyes would be (upper part of the head's front); otherwise the forehead is bare.
rules.note: a no-fringe style, `fringe_id: none`, is a required calibration fixture, §2.9.7

rules.statement: The hair is made of large chunky clumps, not thin strands.
The hairstyle matches the reference hairstyle in shape, length and parting.
rules.hard_note: a consistency check: it ranks and warns, never fails a draft; APP_SPEC S24

rules.statement: The hair looks like a solid 3D volume, not a flat paper cut-out.
Exactly one object is shown, whole, centred, with nothing cropped.
The object is shown from straight in front with no perspective tilt.
The object has no thin strings, chains, rings, holes, spikes or loose floating pieces.
The object matches the accessory in the reference crop in shape, parts and colours.
Lighting is soft and even, with no strong shine, reflections or cast shadow.
The artwork forms one compact shape with a smooth outer edge.
The texture is a flat, evenly lit fabric surface filling the whole image, with no objects, folds or seams.
The image is neutral grey only, with no colour tint.
The grey panel keeps exactly the same outline as the input.
The shading shows a few large soft folds, not busy wrinkles.
All four views show the same object (or hairstyle) with the same parts, colours and proportions.
In the {view} image, the object's front faces the image's {expected} side.
No view adds parts that are absent from the front view and plausible from the concept.
The back view is a believable back of the front design (no face, no front print showing through).
The rendered front view matches the approved front view in silhouette, parts and colours.
The rendered side and back views match the approved views.
There are no floating fragments, holes or broken thin parts.
The surface colours are clean and flat, without smears, baked shine or dark blotches.
Patterns and bands line up across the edges between the front, sides and back.
{print} sits at {region phrase} and is not cut by a body-part edge.
The shoes read as shoes, separate from the trousers.

rules.group: Garment tiles (Gate 2, flat front and back)
rules.statement: The flat front/back shows the same garment design as the concept figure.
rules.note: the flat tile beside the figure crop: block layout, trims and painted details that the user approved at Gate 1; the shirt and pants are composited from the spec, so only this check and the palette check compare them with the picture
rules.hard_note: shown after the first choice; the fix offered to the user, never run automatically: a spec patch, or a different fold or print variant

rules.group: Reference similarity (L14, only when switched on)
rules.statement: The candidate does not reproduce the reference's specific outfit, print, hairstyle or character; shared general style is fine.
